{{short description|American mathematician}}

'''David Saul Jerison''' is an American [[mathematician]] specializing in [[partial differential equation]]s and [[Fourier analysis]]. He is currently a professor of mathematics and a MacVicar Faculty Fellow at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="profile">[https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.html?pid=112 Faculty profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319085435/http://math.mit.edu/people/profile.php?pid=112 |date=2012-03-19 }}, MIT, retrieved 2012-02-21.</ref>

==Education and career==
The son of mathematician [[Meyer Jerison]] and Miriam Schwartz, Jerison did his undergraduate studies at [[Harvard University]] and received a bachelor's degree in 1975. He then received his Ph.D. in 1980 from [[Princeton University]] advised by [[Elias M. Stein]]. After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Chicago]], he joined MIT in 1981.<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=David Saul Jerison|id=8349}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 1985, he received an A.P. [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Foundation Fellowship]] and a [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Calculus 1A: Differentiation | url=https://openlearninglibrary.mit.edu/courses/course-v1:MITx+18.01.1x+2T2019/courseware/cyca/logistics-sequential/ }}</ref> In 1994, Jerison was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich.<ref>Jerison, David. ''Eigenfunctions and harmonic functions in convex and concave domains.'' In: Srishti D. Chatterji (ed.): ''Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians. August 3–11, 1994, Zürich, Switzerland.'' vol. 2. Basel etc., Birkhäuser 1995, {{ISBN|3-7643-5153-5}}, pp. 1108–1117.</ref> In 1999, he was elected as a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|title=Mathematicians Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences|journal=Notices of the AMS|date=September 1999|page=911|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199908/people.pdf}}.</ref> He became a MacVicar Fellow in 2004.<ref name="profile"/> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-26.</ref> In 2012, he received, jointly with [[John M. Lee]], the [[Stefan Bergman Prize]] from the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Jerison and Lee Awarded 2012 Bergman Prize|date=April 2013|author=Jackson, Allyn|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=60|issue=4|pages=497–498|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201304/rnoti-p497.pdf}}</ref>
